slides.claim: The fiscal authorization failure is a two-key problem, not one: a Presidential Directive indemnifying PSU refinery CMDs from personal liability for operating at negative GRM is necessary but insufficient without a simultaneous RBI emergency circular under Section 35A instructing PSU banks to issue sovereign-guaranteed LCs despite exposure concentration norm breaches — without the RBI instrument, crude suppliers receive no payment guarantee and will not load cargoes regardless of CMD indemnification
slides.action_title: RBI Section 35A circular is a co-equal blocking condition, not a follow-on step
slides.subtitle: Legal-operational causal chain; April 2026 crisis scenario; RBI Banking Regulation Act, OFAC/RBI prudential norms

chain.node: Indian basket at $156/bbl → blended GRM estimated −$8 to −$15/bbl
chain.implication: Every VLCC crude cargo LC (~$80–120M notional) issued by SBI/PNB/Bank of Baroda is an unsecured contingent liability against a buyer (PSU refinery) running at negative GRM
chain.blocking_condition: NO — this is the trigger condition

chain.node: Presidential Directive issued to PSU refinery CMDs
chain.implication: CMDs are indemnified from personal liability for authorizing continued operation at negative GRM — they CAN instruct procurement teams to request LCs
chain.blocking_condition: PARTIAL — solves CMD personal liability only; does NOT instruct banks to issue LCs

chain.node: PSU refinery CMD instructs HPCL/BPCL/IOCL treasury to apply for crude cargo LC at SBI/PNB/Bank of Baroda
chain.implication: Bank compliance officer reviews LC application against RBI Master Circular on Credit Risk — DBR.No.Dir.BC.21/13.03.00/2015 and successor circulars — exposure concentration norms prohibit LC issuance to a single operationally insolvent counterparty above 15–25% of bank capital
chain.blocking_condition: YES — RBI statutory exposure norm is a hard block; Presidential Directive has no legal authority over RBI's statutory mandate under Banking Regulation Act Section 35A

chain.node: Bank refuses LC or issues at sub-VLCC scale insufficient for crude cargo
chain.implication: Crude supplier (Aramco, ADNOC, Rosneft trading arm) receives no payment guarantee → will not load cargo → HPCL Mumbai crude inventory continues drawing down toward 7-day trigger
chain.blocking_condition: YES — supply chain physically blocked regardless of CMD indemnification

chain.node: RBI Section 35A emergency circular issued simultaneously with Presidential Directive
chain.implication: RBI formally instructs PSU banks that sovereign-guaranteed LCs up to ₹40,000–50,000 crore aggregate are exempt from standard exposure concentration norms for the duration of the declared emergency — this is within RBI's statutory power under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act
chain.blocking_condition: NO — two-key instrument is complete; bank compliance officers have legal cover to issue LCs

chain.node: Sequential failure mode: RBI circular lags Presidential Directive by 12–24 hours
chain.implication: In the 12–24 hour gap, HPCL Mumbai's treasury team submits LC application; SBI compliance refuses on RBI norm grounds; first emergency cargo loading is delayed; HPCL Mumbai burns 12–24 hours of its 3–5 day remaining buffer; the margin between cargo arrival and shutdown trigger collapses to zero
chain.blocking_condition: YES — 24-hour lag in RBI instrument is sufficient to trigger HPCL Mumbai shutdown sequence per working document H1 evidence_against

key_legal_anchors: Banking Regulation Act 1949, Section 35A: RBI may issue binding directions to any banking company if necessary in public interest or to prevent affairs being conducted in manner detrimental to depositors
RBI Master Circular DBR.No.Dir.BC.21/13.03.00/2015: Exposure norms cap single-counterparty LC exposure — PSU refinery at negative GRM qualifies as stressed counterparty
Presidential Directive authority: Union government power under Article 73 / Essential Commodities Act — does NOT extend to overriding RBI's statutory mandate
Precedent: RBI issued emergency Section 35A directions during IL&FS crisis (2018) and Yes Bank restructuring (2020) — the instrument exists and has been used

playbook_steps.action: PMO designates single crisis cell coordinator (Petroleum Secretary or Cabinet Secretary-level) with explicit written authority to direct MoPNG, Finance Ministry, and RBI simultaneously
playbook_steps.executability: HIGH — no new legislation required; PMO Crisis Management Group structure exists under Cabinet Secretariat (post-2001 Kargil Committee institutional architecture)
playbook_steps.blocking_risk: LOW — purely an executive designation; no parliamentary approval required

playbook_steps.step: T+6 to T+24 hours (parallel track A)
playbook_steps.action: Finance Ministry drafts Presidential Directive indemnifying all six PSU refinery CMDs from personal liability for continued operation at negative GRM — legal basis: Article 73 of Constitution + Essential Commodities Act Section 3 emergency powers
playbook_steps.executability: MEDIUM — Presidential Directive as a formal instrument requires Law Ministry concurrence and Presidential assent; however, in declared emergency, Ministry of Law can fast-track concurrence within 12–18 hours. Precedent: Government of India has issued emergency directions to PSU boards under Essential Commodities Act without full Presidential Directive format — an interim Ministerial Direction from Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) achieves the same CMD indemnification effect within 6–8 hours
playbook_steps.blocking_risk: LOW-MEDIUM — CCEA route is faster and avoids Presidential Directive timeline risk; Law Ministry must confirm within 4 hours which instrument is faster

playbook_steps.step: T+6 to T+24 hours (parallel track B — co-equal, not sequential)
playbook_steps.action: RBI Governor issues Section 35A emergency circular to SBI, PNB, Bank of Baroda, and Canara Bank: sovereign-guaranteed LCs for crude cargo up to ₹40,000–50,000 crore aggregate are exempt from standard single-counterparty exposure concentration norms for 90-day emergency period
playbook_steps.owner: RBI Governor + RBI Department of Banking Regulation
playbook_steps.executability: HIGH — Section 35A directions are within RBI's sole statutory authority; do not require government approval, only government request/consultation. Precedent: RBI issued binding Section 35A directions to Yes Bank within 24 hours (March 5–6, 2020); IL&FS emergency directions issued within 48 hours (October 2018). The instrument is proven, the timeline is feasible
playbook_steps.blocking_risk: LOW — RBI Governor has unilateral authority; the only risk is coordination lag if PMO does not simultaneously brief RBI Governor at T+0. This is the reason the 12-hour PMO designation is the critical path: RBI cannot act without a formal government request framing the emergency

playbook_steps.step: T+24 to T+48 hours — confirmation gate
playbook_steps.action: Crisis cell coordinator confirms both instruments signed and transmitted to: (a) all six refinery CMDs with written acknowledgment, (b) SBI/PNB/Bank of Baroda compliance heads with written LC authorization parameters, (c) PPAC crude procurement cell with LC issuance instructions for first emergency cargo applications
playbook_steps.blocking_risk: MEDIUM — the 6-hour synchronization requirement between Presidential Directive and RBI circular is the operationally critical constraint. If RBI circular lags by more than 6 hours, SBI compliance officers will receive CMD LC requests before they have legal cover to approve them — the first cargo LC application is refused, consuming 12–24 hours of HPCL Mumbai's 3–5 day remaining buffer (Appendix 2)

playbook_steps.action: If RBI circular cannot be confirmed within 6 hours of Presidential Directive issuance, crisis cell must immediately activate supply-side rationing through PSU oil company depot allocation order reductions of 15–20% (Decision 2 fallback) — this extends effective product runway by 3–5 days and preserves the margin for the RBI instrument to catch up without triggering HPCL Mumbai shutdown
playbook_steps.executability: HIGH — PSU oil company depot allocation reductions are within MoPNG direct authority under Essential Commodities Act without state government enforcement machinery; supply-side rationing (reducing depot refills) avoids the panic-buying risk of retail pump caps per working document H7_retail graveyard entry
playbook_steps.blocking_risk: LOW — this is the fallback that makes the overall package executable even if the RBI instrument faces a 12–24 hour delay

proof_content.critical_path_summary: PMO designation (T+12h) → parallel RBI + CCEA drafting (T+12 to T+24h) → simultaneous issuance with max 6h gap (T+24 to T+48h) → LC applications activated (T+48h). Total elapsed time to first cargo LC issuance: 48–54 hours. HPCL Mumbai 7-day trigger breach: T+72 to T+96h. Margin: 18–42 hours — tight but executable if PMO acts at T+0.
